rv.q: Mr. Letts takes scrupulous care to balance laughter and sorrow in exactly the right proportions.
This is now a tighter, sharper and funnier affair.

But let's make an exception in the case of "Superior Donuts," the bracingly funny new play by Tracy Letts, and compare the work in a complimentary way to one of those Golden Age 1970s television comedies by Norman Lear — character-centered, socially and politically alert and, for all the formulaic plotting, brightly entertaining and even occasio...
Superior Donuts may be familiar and unchallenging, but it's also comfortable and no, there's nothing wrong with that.
The mild and predictable seven-character play has transferred intact from Chicago's Steppenwolf Theatre Company.
